entries.body:
বিশ্বস্ত আইনজীবী বাংলাদেশ — এডভোকেট মোঃ শাহ আলম

ফৌজদারি, পারিবারিক, জামিন ও জমি সংক্রান্ত মামলার অভিজ্ঞ আইনজীবী। চেম্বার: উত্তরা, ঢাকা।

আমাদের সম্পর্কে

আমি এডভোকেট মোঃ শাহ আলম — একজন আইনজীবী যিনি শুধু আদালতে লড়েন না, মানুষের পাশে দাঁড়ান। ১০ বছরেরও বেশি সময় ধরে আমি বাংলাদেশের সুপ্রীম কোর্ট থেকে শুরু করে জজ কোর্ট পর্যন্ত হাজারো মানুষের আইনি লড়াইয়ে নিষ্ঠার সাথে তাদের পাশে দাঁড়িয়েছি।

আমি বিশ্বাস করি — আইনি সহায়তা কেবল বিত্তশালীদের জন্য নয়; প্রতিটি সাধারণ মানুষের ন্যায়বিচার পাওয়ার অধিকার রয়েছে। সেই দায়বদ্ধতা থেকেই প্রতিটি মামলায় আমি আমার সর্বোচ্চ চেষ্টা করি।

ফৌজদারি অপরাধ, পারিবারিক বিরোধ, জমিজমা সংক্রান্ত জটিলতা কিংবা করপোরেট আইন — যে কোনো বিষয়ে আপনাকে আইনি প্রক্রিয়াটি সহজ ভাষায় বুঝিয়ে দিয়ে সঠিক সমাধান দিতে আমি প্রতিশ্রুতিবদ্ধ।

"আইন পেশায় আসার পেছনে আমার মূল প্রেরণা ছিল — সাধারণ মানুষকে তাদের অজ্ঞতার কারণে ন্যায়বিচার থেকে বঞ্চিত হতে দেখা। আমার লক্ষ্য সবসময় তাদের পাশে দাঁড়িয়ে আইনি অধিকার নিশ্চিত করা।" — এডভোকেট মোঃ শাহ আলম

আইনি সেবাসমূহ

  • ফৌজদারি মামলার আইনজীবী — ফৌজদারি মামলা, এফআইআর (FIR), জামিন আবেদন এবং ট্রায়াল রিপ্রেজেন্টেশনের জন্য অভিজ্ঞ আইনি পরামর্শ ও সহায়তা। উত্তরা চেম্বার, ঢাকা।
  • বিবাহবিচ্ছেদ ও পারিবারিক আইন — তালাক বা বিবাহবিচ্ছেদ নোটিশ, দেনমোহর ও খোরপোষ, সন্তানের অভিভাবকত্ব এবং পারিবারিক আদালতের মামলা পরিচালনা। উত্তরা চেম্বার, ঢাকা।
  • ভূমি ও সম্পত্তি আইন — জমির মালিকানা নিয়ে বিরোধ, নামজারি (মিউটেশন), দলিল রেজিস্ট্রেশন সংক্রান্ত জটিলতা এবং দেওয়ানি মামলা পরিচালনা। উত্তরা চেম্বার, ঢাকা।
  • জামিন আবেদনের আইনজীবী — দ্রুত জামিনের আবেদন, হাইকোর্টে আগাম জামিন (Anticipatory Bail) এবং সেশন কোর্টে জরুরি জামিনের আইনি পদক্ষেপ।
  • সুপ্রিম কোর্টের আইনজীবী — বাংলাদেশ সুপ্রিম কোর্টের হাইকোর্ট বিভাগ ও আপিল বিভাগে রিট পিটিশন, ফৌজদারি ও দেওয়ানি আপিল এবং রিভিশন মামলা পরিচালনা।
  • কোম্পানি ও কর্পোরেট আইন — কোম্পানি রেজিস্ট্রেশন (RJSC), পার্টনারশিপ ডিড, ট্রেড লাইসেন্স এবং কর্পোরেট আইন সংক্রান্ত যাবতীয় আইনি সহায়তা ও কমপ্লায়েন্স।

আপনার জিজ্ঞাসা (FAQ)

বাংলাদেশে কীভাবে জামিন পাওয়া যায়?

বাংলাদেশে জামিন পেতে হলে উপযুক্ত আদালতে জামিনের আবেদন করতে হয় — অভিযোগের ধরনভেদে সেটি হতে পারে দায়রা আদালত, মহানগর দায়রা আদালত বা হাইকোর্ট বিভাগ। একজন অভিজ্ঞ জামিন আইনজীবী আপনার পক্ষে আবেদন প্রস্তুত করবেন, শক্তিশালী যুক্তি উপস্থাপন করবেন এবং আদালতে আপনার হয়ে লড়বেন। অ-জামিনযোগ্য অপরাধের ক্ষেত্রে হাইকোর্টে যাওয়া প্রয়োজন হতে পারে। জরুরি জামিনের ব্যাপারে এখনই এডভোকেট শাহ আলমের সাথে যোগাযোগ করুন।

বাংলাদেশে বিবাহবিচ্ছেদের প্রক্রিয়া কী?

মুসলিম পরিবারে স্বামী মুসলিম পারিবারিক আইন অধ্যাদেশ ১৯৬১ অনুযায়ী তালাকনামা প্রেরণ করতে পারেন, যা ইউনিয়ন পরিষদ/সিটি কর্পোরেশনের চেয়ারম্যান এবং স্ত্রীর কাছে পাঠাতে হয়। স্ত্রী খুলওয়ার মাধ্যমে (সম্মতিক্রমে) অথবা নিষ্ঠুরতা বা পরিত্যাগের ভিত্তিতে পারিবারিক আদালতে ডিভোর্সের আবেদন করতে পারেন। হিন্দু ও খ্রিষ্টান ধর্মের ক্ষেত্রে আলাদা আইন প্রযোজ্য। উত্তরায় আমাদের চেম্বারে এসে পুরো প্রক্রিয়া সম্পর্কে বিস্তারিত জানুন।

বাংলাদেশে একটি ফৌজদারি মামলা শেষ হতে কতদিন লাগে?

ম্যাজিস্ট্রেট আদালতের সহজ মামলা ৬ থেকে ১৮ মাসে নিষ্পত্তি হতে পারে। দায়রা আদালতের মামলা সাক্ষী ও জটিলতার উপর নির্ভর করে ২ থেকে ৫ বছর পর্যন্ত লাগতে পারে। হাইকোর্টে গেলে আরো বেশি সময় লাগতে পারে। তবে দ্রুত আইনি পদক্ষেপ, শক্তিশালী প্রমাণ এবং একজন দক্ষ আইনজীবী প্রক্রিয়া ত্বরান্বিত করতে সাহায্য করেন।

বাংলাদেশে জমির বিরোধ কীভাবে সমাধান হয়?

বাংলাদেশে জমির বিরোধ দেওয়ানি আদালতে স্বত্ব মামলা, বিভাজন মামলা বা ঘোষণামূলক মামলার মাধ্যমে সমাধান করা হয়। প্রয়োজনীয় কাগজপত্রের মধ্যে থাকে দলিল, নামজারি রেকর্ড, আরএস/বিএস খতিয়ান এবং দখলের প্রমাণ। উত্তরায় আমাদের অভিজ্ঞ জমি বিরোধ আইনজীবী আপনার কাগজপত্র যাচাই করে দ্রুত আইনি পদক্ষেপ নেবেন।

বাংলাদেশে কোম্পানি ও করপোরেট আইনজীবী কী কাজ করেন?

বাংলাদেশে একজন কোম্পানি ও করপোরেট আইনজীবী কোম্পানি আইন ১৯৯৪ অনুযায়ী ব্যবসা নিবন্ধন, অংশীদারিত্ব চুক্তি তৈরি, শেয়ারহোল্ডার বিরোধ নিষ্পত্তি, কর্পোরেট সম্মতি এবং বাণিজ্যিক চুক্তি পর্যালোচনায় সহায়তা করেন। এডভোকেট শাহ আলম ঢাকার ব্যবসায়ী ও উদ্যোক্তাদের তাদের ব্যবসায়িক স্বার্থ রক্ষায় পরামর্শ দিয়ে থাকেন।

বাংলাদেশে একজন আইনজীবীর ফি কত?

বাংলাদেশে আইনজীবীর ফি মামলার ধরন ও আদালতের স্তর অনুযায়ী ভিন্ন হয়। সাধারণ পরামর্শ ফি ৫০০ থেকে ২,০০০ টাকার মধ্যে হয়। জটিল মামলায় হাইকোর্ট ও সুপ্রিম কোর্টে বেশি হতে পারে। এডভোকেট শাহ আলম WhatsApp, ফোন বা সরাসরি চেম্বারে পরামর্শ দেন এবং ফি কাঠামো আগেই স্পষ্টভাবে জানিয়ে দেওয়া হয়। bKash-এ পেমেন্ট গ্রহণযোগ্য: ০১৭১২-৬৫৫৫৪৬।

বাংলাদেশে গ্রেফতার হলে কী করবেন?

আপনি বা আপনার পরিবারের কেউ গ্রেফতার হলে সঙ্গে সঙ্গে একজন ফৌজদারি আইনজীবীর সাথে যোগাযোগ করুন। বাংলাদেশ সংবিধানের ৩৩ অনুচ্ছেদ অনুযায়ী, গ্রেফতার হওয়া প্রতিটি ব্যক্তির অধিকার আছে গ্রেফতারের কারণ জানার এবং নিজের পছন্দের আইনজীবীর সাথে পরামর্শ করার। আইনি পরামর্শ ছাড়া কোনো কাগজে স্বাক্ষর করবেন না। জরুরি জামিন ও আইনি সহায়তার জন্য এখনই WhatsApp-এ এডভোকেট শাহ আলমের সাথে যোগাযোগ করুন।

বাংলাদেশে সাইবার ক্রাইম মামলা কীভাবে পরিচালিত হয়?

বাংলাদেশে সাইবার অপরাধ ডিজিটাল নিরাপত্তা আইন ২০১৮ এবং তথ্য ও যোগাযোগ প্রযুক্তি আইনের আওতায় পরিচালিত হয়। থানায় জিডি করা বা সরাসরি সাইবার ক্রাইম ইউনিটে অভিযোগ দায়ের করা যায়। এ মামলাগুলো সাইবার ট্রাইব্যুনালে বিচার হয়। অভিযোগের মধ্যে থাকতে পারে হ্যাকিং, সামাজিক মাধ্যমে মানহানি, আর্থিক জালিয়াতি এবং পরিচয় চুরি। এডভোকেট শাহ আলম ঢাকার আদালতে সাইবার নিরাপত্তা মামলায় পক্ষে ও বিপক্ষে অভিজ্ঞতাসম্পন্ন।

Trusted Lawyer in Bangladesh – Advocate Md. Shah Alam

Experienced Criminal, Divorce & Bail Lawyer with Chamber in Uttara, Dhaka — Serving Clients Across Bangladesh.

About Advocate Md. Shah Alam

Advocate Md. Shah Alam is a distinguished legal professional with over a decade of experience practicing law at the Supreme Court of Bangladesh. His unwavering commitment to justice has earned him recognition as one of the most trusted advocates in Dhaka.

Specializing in criminal and civil litigation, he has successfully represented clients in high-stakes cases involving complex legal challenges. His approach combines thorough legal research, strategic thinking, and compassionate client service.

Beyond the courtroom, Advocate Shah Alam is passionate about legal education and community service, regularly contributing to legal awareness programs and mentoring young lawyers.

"" —

Practice Areas

  • Criminal Lawyer in Bangladesh — ফৌজদারি মামলা, এফআইআর (FIR), জামিন আবেদন এবং ট্রায়াল রিপ্রেজেন্টেশনের জন্য অভিজ্ঞ আইনি পরামর্শ ও সহায়তা। উত্তরা চেম্বার, ঢাকা।
  • Divorce & Family Lawyer in Bangladesh — Muslim divorce proceedings, child custody, dower (mahr), maintenance, and family court dispute resolution. Available at Uttara chamber.
  • Land & Property Lawyer in Bangladesh — Resolve property disputes, land registration issues, Namjari (mutation) verification, and civil title lawsuits in Bangladesh courts.
  • Bail Lawyer in Bangladesh — Fast regular bail applications, anticipatory bail in the High Court, and emergency bail representation at sessions courts.
  • Supreme Court Lawyer Bangladesh — Writ petitions, High Court appeals, revisions, and constitutional litigation representation in the Supreme Court of Bangladesh.
  • Company & Corporate Law — Company registration (RJSC), trade licensing, director agreements, business formation, and corporate compliance services.

Frequently Asked Legal Questions

How to get bail in Bangladesh?

To get bail in Bangladesh, a bail application must be filed in the appropriate court — either a Sessions Court, Metropolitan Sessions Court, or the High Court Division, depending on the nature of the charge. An experienced bail lawyer in Dhaka will prepare and file the application, present valid grounds (no flight risk, clean record, health conditions), and argue before the judge. For non-bailable offences, the High Court bail process is often required. Contact Adv. Shah Alam for urgent bail matters.

What is divorce procedure in Bangladesh?

For Muslims, a husband may issue a talaq notice under the Muslim Family Laws Ordinance 1961, which must be sent to the Union Parishad/City Corporation chairman and the spouse. A wife may seek divorce via khula (mutual consent) or through family court on grounds like cruelty or desertion. For Hindus and Christians, separate personal laws apply. All divorce procedures require proper legal documentation and often court proceedings. A divorce lawyer in Uttara can guide you through the complete process.

How long does a criminal case take in Bangladesh?

Simple cases in Magistrate Courts may conclude in 6–18 months. Sessions Court cases often take 2–5 years depending on complexity, number of witnesses, and court schedule. Cases reaching the High Court Division can take longer. Prompt legal action, strong evidence preparation, and an experienced criminal lawyer in Uttara can help accelerate the process.

How to solve land dispute cases in Bangladesh?

Land disputes in Bangladesh are resolved through civil courts by filing a title suit, partition suit, or declaration suit. Supporting documents include deed of sale, mutation records, RS/BS khatian, and possession evidence. An experienced land dispute lawyer in Uttara can assess your documents, represent you in court, and pursue swift resolution.

What does a Company & Corporate lawyer do in Bangladesh?

A company and corporate lawyer in Bangladesh helps with business formation under the Companies Act 1994, drafting partnership agreements, shareholder disputes, corporate compliance, and commercial contract review. Advocate Shah Alam advises businesses and entrepreneurs across Dhaka on protecting their commercial interests.

How much does a lawyer charge in Bangladesh?

Lawyer fees in Bangladesh vary by case type and court level. Basic consultation fees typically range from BDT 500–2,000. Court appearance fees depend on the case complexity — simple hearings may start from BDT 2,000–5,000, while complex High Court and Supreme Court cases can range higher. Advocate Shah Alam provides professional consultations via WhatsApp, phone, or in-chamber visit to assess your case. Transparent fee structures are provided upfront. Payment accepted via bKash: 01712655546.

What should I do if I am arrested in Bangladesh?

If you or a family member is arrested in Bangladesh, immediately contact a criminal lawyer. Under Article 33 of the Bangladesh Constitution, an arrested person has the right to be informed of the grounds of arrest and to consult a lawyer of their choice. Do not sign any documents without legal counsel. Contact Advocate Shah Alam immediately via WhatsApp for urgent bail and legal advice — available for emergency consultations.

How are cyber crime cases handled in Bangladesh?

Cyber crimes in Bangladesh are handled under the Digital Security Act 2018 (DSA) and the ICT Act. Cases involve filing GD (General Diary) at the police station or directly with the Cyber Crime Unit. These cases are heard in Cyber Tribunals. Charges can include hacking, social media defamation, financial fraud, and identity theft. Advocate Shah Alam has experience in defending and prosecuting digital security cases in Dhaka courts.

entries.body:
বিশ্বস্ত আইনজীবী বাংলাদেশ — এডভোকেট মোঃ শাহ আলম

ফৌজদারি, পারিবারিক, জামিন ও জমি সংক্রান্ত মামলার অভিজ্ঞ আইনজীবী। চেম্বার: উত্তরা, ঢাকা।

আমাদের সম্পর্কে

আমি এডভোকেট মোঃ শাহ আলম — একজন আইনজীবী যিনি শুধু আদালতে লড়েন না, মানুষের পাশে দাঁড়ান। ১০ বছরেরও বেশি সময় ধরে আমি বাংলাদেশের সুপ্রীম কোর্ট থেকে শুরু করে জজ কোর্ট পর্যন্ত হাজারো মানুষের আইনি লড়াইয়ে নিষ্ঠার সাথে তাদের পাশে দাঁড়িয়েছি।

আমি বিশ্বাস করি — আইনি সহায়তা কেবল বিত্তশালীদের জন্য নয়; প্রতিটি সাধারণ মানুষের ন্যায়বিচার পাওয়ার অধিকার রয়েছে। সেই দায়বদ্ধতা থেকেই প্রতিটি মামলায় আমি আমার সর্বোচ্চ চেষ্টা করি।

ফৌজদারি অপরাধ, পারিবারিক বিরোধ, জমিজমা সংক্রান্ত জটিলতা কিংবা করপোরেট আইন — যে কোনো বিষয়ে আপনাকে আইনি প্রক্রিয়াটি সহজ ভাষায় বুঝিয়ে দিয়ে সঠিক সমাধান দিতে আমি প্রতিশ্রুতিবদ্ধ।

"আইন পেশায় আসার পেছনে আমার মূল প্রেরণা ছিল — সাধারণ মানুষকে তাদের অজ্ঞতার কারণে ন্যায়বিচার থেকে বঞ্চিত হতে দেখা। আমার লক্ষ্য সবসময় তাদের পাশে দাঁড়িয়ে আইনি অধিকার নিশ্চিত করা।" — এডভোকেট মোঃ শাহ আলম

আইনি সেবাসমূহ

  • ফৌজদারি মামলার আইনজীবী — ফৌজদারি মামলা, এফআইআর (FIR), জামিন আবেদন এবং ট্রায়াল রিপ্রেজেন্টেশনের জন্য অভিজ্ঞ আইনি পরামর্শ ও সহায়তা। উত্তরা চেম্বার, ঢাকা।
  • বিবাহবিচ্ছেদ ও পারিবারিক আইন — তালাক বা বিবাহবিচ্ছেদ নোটিশ, দেনমোহর ও খোরপোষ, সন্তানের অভিভাবকত্ব এবং পারিবারিক আদালতের মামলা পরিচালনা। উত্তরা চেম্বার, ঢাকা।
  • ভূমি ও সম্পত্তি আইন — জমির মালিকানা নিয়ে বিরোধ, নামজারি (মিউটেশন), দলিল রেজিস্ট্রেশন সংক্রান্ত জটিলতা এবং দেওয়ানি মামলা পরিচালনা। উত্তরা চেম্বার, ঢাকা।
  • জামিন আবেদনের আইনজীবী — দ্রুত জামিনের আবেদন, হাইকোর্টে আগাম জামিন (Anticipatory Bail) এবং সেশন কোর্টে জরুরি জামিনের আইনি পদক্ষেপ।
  • সুপ্রিম কোর্টের আইনজীবী — বাংলাদেশ সুপ্রিম কোর্টের হাইকোর্ট বিভাগ ও আপিল বিভাগে রিট পিটিশন, ফৌজদারি ও দেওয়ানি আপিল এবং রিভিশন মামলা পরিচালনা।
  • কোম্পানি ও কর্পোরেট আইন — কোম্পানি রেজিস্ট্রেশন (RJSC), পার্টনারশিপ ডিড, ট্রেড লাইসেন্স এবং কর্পোরেট আইন সংক্রান্ত যাবতীয় আইনি সহায়তা ও কমপ্লায়েন্স।

আপনার জিজ্ঞাসা (FAQ)

বাংলাদেশে কীভাবে জামিন পাওয়া যায়?

বাংলাদেশে জামিন পেতে হলে উপযুক্ত আদালতে জামিনের আবেদন করতে হয় — অভিযোগের ধরনভেদে সেটি হতে পারে দায়রা আদালত, মহানগর দায়রা আদালত বা হাইকোর্ট বিভাগ। একজন অভিজ্ঞ জামিন আইনজীবী আপনার পক্ষে আবেদন প্রস্তুত করবেন, শক্তিশালী যুক্তি উপস্থাপন করবেন এবং আদালতে আপনার হয়ে লড়বেন। অ-জামিনযোগ্য অপরাধের ক্ষেত্রে হাইকোর্টে যাওয়া প্রয়োজন হতে পারে। জরুরি জামিনের ব্যাপারে এখনই এডভোকেট শাহ আলমের সাথে যোগাযোগ করুন।

বাংলাদেশে বিবাহবিচ্ছেদের প্রক্রিয়া কী?

মুসলিম পরিবারে স্বামী মুসলিম পারিবারিক আইন অধ্যাদেশ ১৯৬১ অনুযায়ী তালাকনামা প্রেরণ করতে পারেন, যা ইউনিয়ন পরিষদ/সিটি কর্পোরেশনের চেয়ারম্যান এবং স্ত্রীর কাছে পাঠাতে হয়। স্ত্রী খুলওয়ার মাধ্যমে (সম্মতিক্রমে) অথবা নিষ্ঠুরতা বা পরিত্যাগের ভিত্তিতে পারিবারিক আদালতে ডিভোর্সের আবেদন করতে পারেন। হিন্দু ও খ্রিষ্টান ধর্মের ক্ষেত্রে আলাদা আইন প্রযোজ্য। উত্তরায় আমাদের চেম্বারে এসে পুরো প্রক্রিয়া সম্পর্কে বিস্তারিত জানুন।

বাংলাদেশে একটি ফৌজদারি মামলা শেষ হতে কতদিন লাগে?

ম্যাজিস্ট্রেট আদালতের সহজ মামলা ৬ থেকে ১৮ মাসে নিষ্পত্তি হতে পারে। দায়রা আদালতের মামলা সাক্ষী ও জটিলতার উপর নির্ভর করে ২ থেকে ৫ বছর পর্যন্ত লাগতে পারে। হাইকোর্টে গেলে আরো বেশি সময় লাগতে পারে। তবে দ্রুত আইনি পদক্ষেপ, শক্তিশালী প্রমাণ এবং একজন দক্ষ আইনজীবী প্রক্রিয়া ত্বরান্বিত করতে সাহায্য করেন।

বাংলাদেশে জমির বিরোধ কীভাবে সমাধান হয়?

বাংলাদেশে জমির বিরোধ দেওয়ানি আদালতে স্বত্ব মামলা, বিভাজন মামলা বা ঘোষণামূলক মামলার মাধ্যমে সমাধান করা হয়। প্রয়োজনীয় কাগজপত্রের মধ্যে থাকে দলিল, নামজারি রেকর্ড, আরএস/বিএস খতিয়ান এবং দখলের প্রমাণ। উত্তরায় আমাদের অভিজ্ঞ জমি বিরোধ আইনজীবী আপনার কাগজপত্র যাচাই করে দ্রুত আইনি পদক্ষেপ নেবেন।

বাংলাদেশে কোম্পানি ও করপোরেট আইনজীবী কী কাজ করেন?

বাংলাদেশে একজন কোম্পানি ও করপোরেট আইনজীবী কোম্পানি আইন ১৯৯৪ অনুযায়ী ব্যবসা নিবন্ধন, অংশীদারিত্ব চুক্তি তৈরি, শেয়ারহোল্ডার বিরোধ নিষ্পত্তি, কর্পোরেট সম্মতি এবং বাণিজ্যিক চুক্তি পর্যালোচনায় সহায়তা করেন। এডভোকেট শাহ আলম ঢাকার ব্যবসায়ী ও উদ্যোক্তাদের তাদের ব্যবসায়িক স্বার্থ রক্ষায় পরামর্শ দিয়ে থাকেন।

বাংলাদেশে একজন আইনজীবীর ফি কত?

বাংলাদেশে আইনজীবীর ফি মামলার ধরন ও আদালতের স্তর অনুযায়ী ভিন্ন হয়। সাধারণ পরামর্শ ফি ৫০০ থেকে ২,০০০ টাকার মধ্যে হয়। জটিল মামলায় হাইকোর্ট ও সুপ্রিম কোর্টে বেশি হতে পারে। এডভোকেট শাহ আলম WhatsApp, ফোন বা সরাসরি চেম্বারে পরামর্শ দেন এবং ফি কাঠামো আগেই স্পষ্টভাবে জানিয়ে দেওয়া হয়। bKash-এ পেমেন্ট গ্রহণযোগ্য: ০১৭১২-৬৫৫৫৪৬।

বাংলাদেশে গ্রেফতার হলে কী করবেন?

আপনি বা আপনার পরিবারের কেউ গ্রেফতার হলে সঙ্গে সঙ্গে একজন ফৌজদারি আইনজীবীর সাথে যোগাযোগ করুন। বাংলাদেশ সংবিধানের ৩৩ অনুচ্ছেদ অনুযায়ী, গ্রেফতার হওয়া প্রতিটি ব্যক্তির অধিকার আছে গ্রেফতারের কারণ জানার এবং নিজের পছন্দের আইনজীবীর সাথে পরামর্শ করার। আইনি পরামর্শ ছাড়া কোনো কাগজে স্বাক্ষর করবেন না। জরুরি জামিন ও আইনি সহায়তার জন্য এখনই WhatsApp-এ এডভোকেট শাহ আলমের সাথে যোগাযোগ করুন।

বাংলাদেশে সাইবার ক্রাইম মামলা কীভাবে পরিচালিত হয়?

বাংলাদেশে সাইবার অপরাধ ডিজিটাল নিরাপত্তা আইন ২০১৮ এবং তথ্য ও যোগাযোগ প্রযুক্তি আইনের আওতায় পরিচালিত হয়। থানায় জিডি করা বা সরাসরি সাইবার ক্রাইম ইউনিটে অভিযোগ দায়ের করা যায়। এ মামলাগুলো সাইবার ট্রাইব্যুনালে বিচার হয়। অভিযোগের মধ্যে থাকতে পারে হ্যাকিং, সামাজিক মাধ্যমে মানহানি, আর্থিক জালিয়াতি এবং পরিচয় চুরি। এডভোকেট শাহ আলম ঢাকার আদালতে সাইবার নিরাপত্তা মামলায় পক্ষে ও বিপক্ষে অভিজ্ঞতাসম্পন্ন।

Professional Career

Privacy Policy | Advocate Md. Shah Alam

Last updated: May 18, 2026

1. Introduction

Welcome to advmdshahalam.me ("Website"), operated by Advocate Md. Shah Alam ("we", "us", or "our"). We are dedicated to maintaining the confidentiality and integrity of personal information. This Privacy Policy details how we collect, use, disclose, and safeguard user data when you access or use our website.

2. Information We Collect

We may collect personal details that you voluntarily submit through our consultation form, email, or WhatsApp, including your name, contact phone number, email address, and summary of your legal inquiry. In addition, we collect automated browsing data such as IP address, browser type, referral URLs, operating system, and pages viewed.

3. How We Use Your Information

Information gathered is utilized to respond directly to client consultations, provide legal assistance, monitor and improve site performance, analyze traffic metrics, and present relevant advertisements.

4. Google AdSense & Advertising Cookie Policy

This Website uses Google AdSense, a third-party advertising service provided by Google LLC (1600 Amphitheatre Parkway, Mountain View, CA 94043, USA). Google and its third-party advertising partners utilize cookies—including the DoubleClick DART cookie—to serve advertisements to users based on their prior visits to this website and other websites across the Internet.

Third-party advertising vendors and ad networks display advertisements on advmdshahalam.me. These cookies enable Google and its network partners to show targeted ads tailored to user browsing history. We do not control cookies placed by Google AdSense.

Opt-Out: Users may opt out of personalized advertising at any time by visiting Google Ads Settings or through the Digital Advertising Alliance opt-out portal. You may also adjust cookie preferences directly in your browser settings.

Bail Lawyer in Bangladesh

⚠️ Legal Disclaimer: This article provides general legal information only and does not constitute legal advice. For advice specific to your situation, consult Advocate Md. Shah Alam directly at +880 1712-655546.

Getting bail in Bangladesh requires expert legal representation. Advocate Md. Shah Alam specialises in bail applications at all court levels — from Magistrate Court to the Supreme Court of Bangladesh.

Types of Bail We Handle

  • Regular Bail: Filed in Magistrate or Sessions Court for bailable and non-bailable offences
  • Anticipatory Bail: Filed in High Court before arrest — protects you from being taken into custody
  • High Court Bail: For cases rejected at lower courts or involving serious offences
  • Temporary/Interim Bail: Emergency bail for urgent situations

Bail Process in Bangladesh

A bail application is filed with supporting documents (FIR copy, charge sheet if available, personal particulars). The lawyer presents grounds such as clean record, family ties, and no flight risk. For serious offences, the application goes to High Court.

Section 138 NI Act Bangladesh: Complete Guide to Cheque Dishonour Cases

By Advocate Md. Shah Alam · 2026-07-12 · 11 min read

⚠️ Legal Disclaimer: This article provides general legal information only and does not constitute legal advice. For advice specific to your situation, consult Advocate Md. Shah Alam directly at +880 1712-655546.

Cheque dishonour cases under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 are among the most frequently litigated matters in Bangladesh's courts. Whether you are a creditor seeking to recover money from a defaulting party or an accused defending a cheque case, understanding the legal framework, procedural requirements, and available defences is critical. What Is Section 138 NI Act in Bangladesh?

Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 creates a criminal offence for the dishonour of a cheque issued for the discharge of a legally enforceable debt or liability. The section was introduced to enhance the credibility of cheque transactions in commerce and protect payees from fraud.

The law applies when a cheque is returned by the bank unpaid because:

  • The amount in the account is insufficient to honour the payment;
  • The amount exceeds the arrangement made with the bank;
  • The account has been closed;
  • A stop-payment instruction was issued by the drawer fraudulently.

It is important to understand that Section 138 is a criminal provision, not merely a civil remedy. A conviction carries criminal penalties including imprisonment. This dual nature — civil debt recovery combined with criminal prosecution — makes it a powerful tool for creditors in Bangladesh.

However, the law also provides safeguards against misuse. The cheque must have been issued for a legally enforceable debt or liability. Cheques given as gifts, security deposits (in some interpretations), or post-dated cheques that do not represent an existing liability may not attract Section 138 liability.

Essential Elements of a Section 138 Offence

For a Section 138 complaint to succeed, the complainant (payee) must establish all of the following essential elements:

  1. The Cheque Was Drawn: The accused (drawer) must have actually drawn the cheque on their bank account.
  2. The Cheque Was Presented: The payee must have presented the cheque to their bank within the period of its validity (generally 6 months from the date of issue).
  3. The Cheque Was Dishonoured: The cheque must have been returned unpaid by the bank, evidenced by a dishonour memo or bank return memo.
  4. The Cheque Was Issued for a Legally Enforceable Debt: The underlying transaction must be a legal one — a loan, sale of goods, services, or a recognised financial obligation.
  5. A Demand Notice Was Sent: The payee must have sent a written demand notice to the drawer within 30 days of receiving the bank's dishonour memo.
  6. Failure to Make Payment: The drawer must have failed to make the payment within 30 days of receiving the notice.
  7. Complaint Filed Within Time: The complaint in court must be filed within 30 days of the expiry of the notice period.

Failure to establish even one of these elements can result in acquittal. Courts apply these requirements strictly, so both complainants and accused must pay careful attention to each step in the chain.

The 30-Day Notice Requirement: A Critical Step

The legal demand notice is perhaps the most critical procedural step in a Section 138 case, and a vast number of cases fail because this step is not carried out correctly. Here is what the law requires:

  • Timing: The notice must be sent within 30 days of the date of receipt of the bank's dishonour memo (also called the cheque return memo).
  • Form: The notice must be in writing. Oral demands do not satisfy this requirement.
  • Content: The notice must clearly state that the cheque was dishonoured, the amount due, the date of the cheque, and a specific demand for payment within 30 days of receipt of the notice.
  • Mode of Service: The notice should be sent by registered post with acknowledgement due (AD) to the drawer's last known address. This creates a legal presumption of service. Sending by email alone is insufficient unless supplemented by postal notice.
  • Proof of Sending: Keep the postal receipt, the registered post slip, and the returned acknowledgement card (even if the notice is refused).

What if the drawer refuses to accept the notice? If the drawer deliberately avoids receiving the notice, courts have held that this does not defeat the notice requirement. Service is deemed complete when the letter is tendered at the correct address, even if refused.

After the 30-day notice period expires without payment, the payee has another 30 days to file the criminal complaint in court. Missing this window extinguishes the right to file a Section 138 case. Consult a criminal lawyer in Bangladesh immediately upon receiving a dishonour memo to ensure these timelines are met.

How to File a Cheque Dishonour Case in Court

Once the notice period has expired and the drawer has failed to pay, the payee can initiate criminal proceedings by filing a complaint. The process is as follows:

  1. Engage a Lawyer: Retain a criminal or commercial lawyer with experience in NI Act cases to draft the complaint.
  2. Prepare the Complaint: Draft a formal written complaint (ejahar) setting out all the facts — the original transaction, the cheque details, the dishonour, the notice, and the failure to pay.
  3. Choose the Correct Court: In Bangladesh, Section 138 cases are filed before the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate (CMM) in city areas (Dhaka, Chattogram, etc.) or the Chief Judicial Magistrate (CJM) in other districts. Jurisdiction lies where the bank branch that dishonoured the cheque is located.
  4. Attach Documents: File the complaint with the original dishonoured cheque, the bank's dishonour memo, copies of the demand notice, postal receipts, and proof of service.
  5. Court Takes Cognisance: The Magistrate examines the complaint and, if satisfied that a prima facie case exists, takes cognisance of the offence and issues a summons to the accused drawer.
  6. Trial Proceedings: The case is tried as a criminal case. The complainant presents evidence (witnesses and documents) and the accused is given the opportunity to cross-examine and present a defence.
  7. Judgment: If convicted, the court imposes punishment. If acquitted, the accused is discharged.

Punishment and Penalties Under Section 138

Section 138 of the NI Act prescribes both imprisonment and fines as punishments, making cheque dishonour a cognisable criminal matter in Bangladesh:

  • Imprisonment: The convicted drawer may be sentenced to imprisonment for a term which may extend to one (1) year.
  • Fine: A fine which may extend to three times the amount of the cheque — this is a significant financial penalty designed to act as a deterrent and compensate the payee.
  • Both: The court may impose both imprisonment and a fine simultaneously.

Courts in Bangladesh have increasingly leaned towards imposing fines rather than custodial sentences in commercial disputes, especially where the accused shows genuine willingness to settle. However, in cases involving repeated dishonour or deliberate fraud, imprisonment is not uncommon.

Beyond criminal penalties, the conviction also:

  • Creates a criminal record for the drawer;
  • Can affect the drawer's ability to obtain credit, business licences, and professional registrations;
  • May trigger civil recovery proceedings simultaneously in a separate civil court for recovery of the cheque amount plus interest.

Given these consequences, accused persons should immediately consult a criminal lawyer in Dhaka upon receiving summons in a Section 138 case.

Common Defences Against a Section 138 Case

An accused drawer is not without recourse. Bangladesh courts recognise several valid defences that, if properly established, can result in acquittal:

  • Cheque Not Issued for a Legally Enforceable Debt: If the cheque was issued as a security, a gift, or for an illegal transaction (such as gambling debt or usurious loan), it cannot found a Section 138 case.
  • Notice Not Sent in Time: If the payee failed to send the demand notice within 30 days of receiving the dishonour memo, the complaint is barred.
  • Notice Not Properly Served: A notice sent to the wrong address or without registered post may be challenged.
  • Complaint Filed Out of Time: If the complaint was filed after the 30-day window following the notice period, it is time-barred and must be dismissed.
  • Cheque Presented After Validity Period: A cheque presented to the bank after 6 months from its date is stale and dishonour of such a cheque does not attract Section 138.
  • Cheque Was Stolen or Forged: If the cheque was issued under forgery, coercion, or was stolen without the drawer's knowledge, this is a complete defence.
  • Payment Already Made: If the drawer can show that the debt was discharged before or after the notice period, and the complainant continues the case in bad faith, this can be raised as a defence.

Mounting a successful defence requires thorough preparation and documentation. An experienced criminal lawyer can evaluate which defences apply to your specific situation and prepare the evidence accordingly.

How a Lawyer Can Help You Win or Settle

Whether you are the complainant trying to recover money or the accused trying to defend yourself, having a skilled criminal lawyer in Bangladesh by your side makes a decisive difference in Section 138 cases. Here is how:

  • For Complainants: A lawyer ensures that the notice is sent correctly and on time, the complaint is drafted with all material particulars, the right court is approached, and evidence is presented effectively during trial.
  • For Accused: A lawyer analyses the complaint for procedural defects (late notice, wrong court, time bar), negotiates a settlement or payment plan with the complainant to avoid conviction, and vigorously cross-examines the complainant's witnesses to expose weaknesses in their case.
  • Mediation and Compromise: In many cases, a negotiated settlement — where the accused pays the cheque amount plus compensation — results in compounding of the offence and withdrawal of the complaint. This avoids a criminal conviction and saves both parties the cost and time of a full trial.
  • Appeals: If convicted by the Magistrate, the accused can appeal to the Sessions Court, the High Court Division, and ultimately the Appellate Division. A lawyer experienced in Supreme Court proceedings is essential for higher appellate stages.

Frequently Asked Questions

Can I file a civil suit for recovery of money alongside a Section 138 criminal case?

Yes. Filing a Section 138 criminal complaint does not bar you from simultaneously filing a civil suit for recovery of the cheque amount, interest, and damages. Both proceedings can run concurrently. Many creditors pursue both to maximise recovery and pressure.

What if the cheque was given as a security deposit — does Section 138 still apply?

This is a contested area of law in Bangladesh. Courts have held in some cases that a cheque given merely as security (not against an existing legally enforceable debt) may not attract Section 138 liability. The accused must raise this as a defence and produce evidence to show the cheque's purpose was security, not payment.

If I am the accused, should I pay the amount after receiving the court summons?

Paying the amount does not automatically close the case. However, if you reach a written compromise with the complainant and they file a petition for compounding and withdrawal, the court can allow withdrawal of the case. Consult a lawyer before making any payment to ensure you receive proper legal protection.

Can a Section 138 NI Act case be settled out of court?

Yes. Section 138 is a compoundable offence under Bangladesh law, meaning the complainant can compound (settle) the matter and apply for withdrawal at any stage before conviction. A negotiated settlement is common and practical in commercial cheque disputes.

How long does a Section 138 case take to conclude in Bangladesh?

Depending on court workload, a Section 138 case can take anywhere from 6 months to 3–4 years at the trial court level. Cases involving multiple adjournments or complex defences take longer. An experienced lawyer can help expedite proceedings where possible.

Administrative Tribunal Bangladesh: Government Service Lawsuits, Dismissal & Pension Guide

By Advocate Md. Shah Alam · 2026-11-08 · 19 minutes

⚠️ Legal Disclaimer: This article provides general legal information only and does not constitute legal advice. For advice specific to your situation, consult Advocate Md. Shah Alam directly at +880 1712-655546.

For civil servants, government officers, public school educators, and employees of autonomous statutory corporations in Bangladesh, public service is governed by specialized constitutional and statutory protections. When a government employee is subjected to wrongful dismissal, compulsory retirement, punitive demotion, arbitrary transfer, supersession in promotion, or withholding of pension and gratuity benefits, ordinary civil courts lack jurisdiction. Under Article 117 of the Constitution of Bangladesh and the Administrative Tribunals Act 1980 (Act No. VII of 1981), exclusive judicial jurisdiction to adjudicate terms and conditions of public service resides with the Administrative Tribunal and the Administrative Appellate Tribunal. This comprehensive legal guide by Advocate Md. Shah Alam, Supreme Court Advocate and administrative litigation specialist in Dhaka, details the statutory framework, departmental appeal prerequisites, limitation deadlines, and litigation strategies before the Administrative Tribunals and Supreme Court.

1. Constitutional Mandate: Article 117 & Act No. VII of 1981

In the legal structure of Bangladesh, public employment is treated not as a private master-servant contract, but as a public status safeguarded by the Constitution. Under Article 117(1) of the Constitution of Bangladesh, Parliament is empowered to establish Administrative Tribunals to exercise exclusive jurisdiction in respect of matters relating to the terms and conditions of persons in the service of the Republic.

To implement this constitutional guarantee, Parliament enacted the Administrative Tribunals Act 1980 (Act No. VII of 1981). Section 4 of the Act vests exclusive original jurisdiction in Administrative Tribunals to hear and determine applications made by public servants regarding their service conditions, disciplinary punishments, pensions, and statutory rights. Under Article 117(2), once an Administrative Tribunal is established for a matter, no other court—including the High Court Division under Article 102 writ jurisdiction—can entertain proceedings regarding that matter, subject to very narrow exceptions concerning vires of statutes or patent absence of jurisdiction.

This makes the Administrative Tribunal the indispensable judicial battleground for any civil servant seeking redress against arbitrary government action. The presiding member of the Tribunal is a senior judicial officer (typically of the rank of District Judge), ensuring impartial judicial scrutiny over executive excesses.

2. Jurisdiction: Who Can File Before the Administrative Tribunal?

Understanding which categories of employees fall within the protective umbrella of the Administrative Tribunal is vital before filing an application:

  • Persons in the Service of the Republic: All members of the Bangladesh Civil Service (BCS) cadres, administrative officers, ministry officials, magistracy staff, police personnel, and non-cadre government employees holding posts in government directorates and departments.
  • Statutory Public Authorities: Employees of statutory bodies, corporations, and state institutions established by act of Parliament (such as Bangladesh Power Development Board, WASA, RAJUK, and nationalized banks) where the relevant service rules notify tribunal jurisdiction.
  • Retired Civil Servants & Pensioners: Former public servants whose post-retirement pension, gratuity, general provident fund (GPF), or medical allowances are unlawfully withheld or delayed.
  • Excluded Categories: Members of the Defense Forces (Army, Navy, Air Force) governed by their respective military acts, and staff of the Supreme Court of Bangladesh, who are excluded under Section 3 of the Act.

3. The Mandatory Departmental Appeal Prerequisite

A critical procedural trap that causes many administrative service lawsuits to be dismissed at the threshold is failure to exhaust internal administrative remedies. Under Section 4(2) of the Administrative Tribunals Act 1980, the Tribunal is statutorily barred from entertaining an application unless the applicant has first exhausted all departmental appeals, representations, or reviews available under applicable service rules.

Under the Government Servants (Discipline and Appeal) Rules 2018:

  1. When a punishing authority passes an adverse disciplinary order (such as dismissal, removal, reduction in rank, or stoppage of increment), the employee must submit a formal Departmental Appeal within thirty (30) days to the designated appellate authority (e.g. Secretary of the Ministry or Director General).
  2. The departmental appeal must clearly state the procedural irregularities of the inquiry, violation of natural justice, and substantive defenses.
  3. If the appellate authority rejects the appeal, the prerequisite is met.
  4. The Two-Month Rule: If the appellate authority fails to render a decision within two (2) months from the date of filing the departmental appeal, Section 4(2) allows the employee to treat the appeal as constructively exhausted and approach the Administrative Tribunal directly.

4. Strict Limitation Windows Under Section 4 of the Act

Facing a government service dispute, dismissal or pension withholding? Contact our administrative law chamber on WhatsApp at +880 1955-802007. We represent public servants across all ministries.

Limitation in public service litigation is strictly enforced. The Administrative Tribunals Act 1980 does not allow for indefinite delays, and Section 5 of the Limitation Act 1908 cannot be casually invoked to condone gross negligence.

The statutory limitation rules under Section 4(2) dictate that an application must be filed before the Administrative Tribunal within:

  • Six (6) Months from Appeal Decision: If the departmental appellate authority delivers a formal written order rejecting or modifying the appeal, the case must be filed within precisely six months from the date of communication of that order.
  • Six Months Following the Two-Month Silence Window: If the departmental authority sits on the appeal without passing an order, the case must be filed within six months immediately following the expiry of the initial two-month waiting period (i.e. between month 2 and month 8 from the appeal filing date).

Filing even one day after the statutory limitation deadline results in threshold dismissal of the application. An advocate must verify postal tracking receipts and service delivery memos before drafting the petition.

6. Grounds for Challenging Departmental Inquiries & Penalties

When challenging disciplinary punishments—such as dismissal, removal from service, compulsory retirement, or reduction in pay scale—the Administrative Tribunal scrutinizes whether the administrative inquiry complied with natural justice and statutory rules.

Established grounds for quashing disciplinary orders include:

  • Denial of Natural Justice: The employee was denied an adequate opportunity to submit a written statement of defense, examine prosecution documents, or cross-examine witnesses who testified against them.
  • Biased Inquiry Officer: The departmental inquiry officer was a subordinate of the complainant or demonstrated open prejudice during the inquiry proceedings.
  • Failure to Supply Inquiry Report: The punishing authority failed to serve a copy of the inquiry officer's report along with a second show-cause notice prior to imposing the final penalty, depriving the employee of the right to rebut adverse findings.
  • Disproportionate Penalty: Imposing capital administrative punishment (dismissal or removal) for minor administrative oversights violates the established doctrine of proportionality recognized by the Supreme Court of Bangladesh.

7. Remedies for Withheld Pension, Gratuity & Retirement Benefits

One of the most frequent grievances presented by senior public servants and their families involves the arbitrary withholding of post-retirement pension, gratuity, and leave encashment benefits. Decades of Supreme Court precedent, including landmark decisions of the Appellate Division, affirm that pension is not a bounty or charitable grace; it is property earned through long, honorable service protected under Article 42 of the Constitution.

Key principles enforced by the Administrative Tribunal include:

  1. No Withholding Without Judicial Conviction: Government departments cannot freeze or withhold pension or gratuity benefits based on preliminary audit objections, administrative inquiries, or unadjudicated departmental allegations that were never concluded during the officer's active service.
  2. Post-Retirement Disciplinary Inquiries Barred: Under the Public Servants (Retirement) Act 1974, once an officer has formally retired and crossed the statutory retirement age, new departmental disciplinary proceedings cannot be instituted without explicit statutory authorization.
  3. Release of Family Pension: In the event of a public servant's death, surviving spouses and minor dependents can approach the Tribunal to secure immediate release of family pension and welfare benefits unlawfully held up by the Controller General of Accounts (CGA).

8. Appeals to Administrative Appellate Tribunal & Supreme Court

The decisions of the Administrative Tribunal are subject to a structured statutory appellate hierarchy centered in Dhaka:

  • The Administrative Appellate Tribunal (AAT): Established under Section 5 of the Act and sitting in Dhaka, the AAT comprises a Chairman (who is or has been a Judge of the Supreme Court or is qualified to be such) and two member colleagues. An aggrieved public servant or the Government can file an appeal before the AAT within three (3) months from the date of the Administrative Tribunal's judgment under Section 6. The AAT has powers to confirm, modify, or reverse the tribunal's order.
  • Appellate Division of the Supreme Court (CPLA): Under Section 6A of the Act and Article 103 of the Constitution, no appeal lies from the AAT to the High Court Division. The sole avenue of further challenge is filing a Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal (CPLA) directly before the Appellate Division of the Supreme Court of Bangladesh within thirty (30) days.
  • Execution of Decrees: Under Section 10A, the orders of the Administrative Tribunal and AAT are enforceable throughout Bangladesh as decrees of a civil court, compelling recalcitrant ministries to execute reinstatements and disburse funds.

9. Illustrative Scenario: Overturning Wrongful Compulsory Retirement

Illustrative scenario (composite; names and details changed): A senior deputy secretary serving in a government ministry in Dhaka was abruptly served with a compulsory retirement order under Section 9(2) of the Public Servants (Retirement) Act 1974 after 26 years of distinguished service. The order cited 'public interest' but was triggered by the officer's refusal to approve an irregular public procurement tender favored by politically influential contractors. No formal charge sheet or inquiry had ever been conducted.

Faced with loss of dignity and severe pension reductions, the officer retained Advocate Md. Shah Alam's chamber. Our legal team executed a structured administrative challenge:

  1. Drafted and submitted a comprehensive Departmental Review Petition to the Senior Secretary of the Ministry of Public Administration within thirty days, demonstrating the officer's unblemished Annual Confidential Report (ACR) record and proving that the procurement objection was grounded in statutory financial rules.
  2. When the ministry remained silent for two months, treated the appeal as constructively exhausted under Section 4(2) of the Administrative Tribunals Act 1980 and filed an Administrative Tribunal Case before the Administrative Tribunal, Dhaka.
  3. Argued before the District Judge presiding over the Tribunal that retiring an officer prematurely under the guise of 'public interest' as a disguised punishment without an inquiry violates the landmark principles of natural justice and Supreme Court precedents.
  4. The Administrative Tribunal delivered judgment declaring the compulsory retirement order unlawful, quashing the notification, and directing the ministry to reinstate the officer with full retroactive seniority and back pay.
  5. When the ministry appealed to the Administrative Appellate Tribunal, our advocates defended the decree, securing a complete dismissal of the government's appeal and prompt treasury disbursement of all arrears.

10. Talk to an Advocate: Administrative Service Representation

If you are a civil servant, statutory corporation employee, or retired public officer facing disciplinary penalties, promotion deprivation, or withheld pension benefits in Bangladesh, professional advocacy before the Administrative Tribunals is essential. Advocate Md. Shah Alam and his dedicated team of Supreme Court advocates provide complete representation from departmental appeal drafting to Supreme Court litigation.

Need an advocate for this matter in Bangladesh? Send your documents on WhatsApp to +880 1955-802007, or call +880 1712-655546. Overseas clients: a first document review can be done remotely.

Our principal chamber is located in Uttara, Dhaka, minutes from Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport, alongside our daily litigation chamber at the Supreme Court Bar Association and Dhaka Judge Court.

Frequently Asked Questions

Can I file a case in the Administrative Tribunal without a departmental appeal?

No. Under Section 4(2) of the Administrative Tribunals Act 1980, exhausting all available departmental appeals or reviews is a mandatory statutory prerequisite. Filing without exhausting internal appeals will result in threshold dismissal.

What is the time limit to file a case in the Administrative Tribunal?

Under Section 4(2), the application must be filed within six (6) months from the date of the departmental appeal decision, or within six months after waiting two months for an undecided appeal.

Can an ordinary civil court hear a government employee service case?

No. Under Article 117 of the Constitution and Section 4 of Act No. VII of 1981, Administrative Tribunals have exclusive jurisdiction. Ordinary Assistant Judge and Joint District Judge courts are statutorily barred.

Can the Administrative Tribunal reinstate a dismissed employee with back pay?

Yes. The Administrative Tribunal possesses full judicial powers to set aside wrongful dismissals, quash disciplinary orders, and direct the government to reinstate the employee with retroactive seniority and full salary arrears.

Can the government withhold pension benefits for audit objections?

Under established Supreme Court precedents, pension is a property right earned through service and cannot be withheld for unresolved audit objections unless a formal judicial conviction for financial defalcation exists.

Where do I appeal if the Administrative Tribunal rules against me?

An appeal must be filed within three (3) months before the Administrative Appellate Tribunal (AAT) in Dhaka under Section 6 of the Administrative Tribunals Act 1980.

Can a High Court Writ Petition be filed directly for service matters?

Generally, no, because Article 117(2) bars writ jurisdiction where an Administrative Tribunal exists. Writs are admitted only in narrow instances challenging the constitutional validity of service laws or where the tribunal has no jurisdiction.

Can family members of a deceased government servant file a tribunal case?

Yes. Legal heirs and dependent family members can file an application before the Administrative Tribunal to claim withheld family pensions, gratuities, GPF balances, and statutory death benefits.

Adopting a Child in Bangladesh for NRBs & Foreign Citizens: Family Court Guardianship & Visa Guide (2026)

By Advocate Md. Shah Alam · 2026-11-02 · 19 min read

⚠️ Legal Disclaimer: This article provides general legal information only and does not constitute legal advice. For advice specific to your situation, consult Advocate Md. Shah Alam directly at +880 1712-655546.

For childless Non-Resident Bangladeshi (NRB) couples and foreign nationals residing in the United States, United Kingdom, Canada, or Australia, adopting a child from Bangladesh is a deeply cherished humanitarian aspiration. However, navigating Bangladesh's legal landscape requires an immediate understanding of a foundational jurisprudential reality: **Islamic personal law, which governs the majority of Bangladesh's population, does not recognize the concept of complete, irrevocable 'adoption' (Kafala / দত্তক) in the Western sense of severing original biological parentage.** Instead, Bangladesh facilitates intercountry adoption exclusively through the legal mechanism of **Statutory Guardianship under the Guardians and Wards Act, 1890** adjudicated by the Family Court. Converting this Family Court guardianship decree into a valid overseas immigrant visa (such as the US IR-3 / IR-4 or IH-3 / IH-4 visa, UK Adoption Order, or Canadian intercountry citizenship) demands precise coordination between Family Courts, the Ministry of Social Welfare, the Special Branch of Police, and foreign consular immigration departments. This master guide provides the definitive legal roadmap to securing lawful guardianship, home study clearances, government No Objection Certificates (NOC), and international child emigration.

: · Divorce & Family Court Lawyer in Bangladesh

  2. 2. Statutory Basis: Guardians and Wards Act 1890 & Family Courts Act 2023
  3. 3. Step-by-Step Procedure for Overseas Couples to Obtain Child Guardianship
  4. 4. Home Study Report & International Psychological / Financial Vetting
  5. 5. The Deed of Surrender (সমর্পণ দলিল) vs Institutional Orphanage Custody
  6. 6. Summary Matrix: Guardianship Stages, Timelines & Regulatory Authorities
  7. 7. Securing the Ministry of Social Welfare No Objection Certificate (NOC)
  8. 8. Foreign Visa Protocols: US Embassy (IR-3/IR-4), UK Home Office & Canada IRCC
  9. 9. Converting Bangladeshi Guardianship into a Full Western Adoption Decree
  10. 10. Real-Life Case Study: US-Bangladeshi Couple Adopting from Dhaka to Texas
  11. 11. Fatal Legal Traps: Informal Informal Child Handover & Human Trafficking Risks
  12. 12. Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs)

1. Jurisprudential Framework: Adoption vs Legal Guardianship in Bangladesh

In Western common law jurisdictions (such as the USA, UK, Canada, and Australia), an adoption order legally terminates all parental rights and obligations of the biological parents, permanently creating a new parent-child relationship as if the child had been born biologically to the adoptive parents. In contrast, under Bangladeshi Muslim personal law, a biological father's lineage cannot be erased or substituted. This principle is grounded in Islamic jurisprudence regarding Kafala (caregiving without lineage falsification).

However, Bangladeshi statutory law solves this challenge for international and domestic families through the Guardians and Wards Act, 1890 (Act No. VIII of 1890). Under this statute, prospective adoptive parents (PAPs) are appointed as the Legal Guardians of the Person and Property of the Minor Child with full, exclusive parental authority. The Family Court grants the guardians complete custody, care, control, education, and upbringing rights, explicitly permitting them to relocate the child permanently to their foreign country of residence.

2. Statutory Basis: Guardians and Wards Act 1890 & Family Courts Act 2023

Cross-border child adoption and guardianship proceedings in Bangladesh operate within three foundational legislative pillars:

  1. Section 7 & 10 of the Guardians and Wards Act, 1890: Section 7 empowers the court to appoint a guardian where it is satisfied that doing so is for the 'welfare of the minor'. Section 10 outlines the mandatory contents of the guardianship application (plaint), including the age, religion, residence of the minor, and background of the proposed guardians.
  2. Family Courts Act, 2023 (Act No. 34 of 2023): Vests exclusive original subject-matter jurisdiction over all child guardianship and custody applications in the Family Court (presided over by a Senior Assistant Judge or Assistant Judge).
  3. Ministry of Social Welfare Intercountry Adoption Guidelines: Mandates social welfare scrutiny and police Special Branch verification before an adopted minor can be issued a Bangladeshi passport or taken abroad.

3. Step-by-Step Procedure for Overseas Couples to Obtain Child Guardianship

Prospective parents residing in the US, UK, Canada, or Australia must follow this rigorous, sequential procedural roadmap:

  1. Step 1: Identifying the Child Lawfully: The child must be identified through a licensed government baby home (Chhotomoni Nibas), an authorized non-governmental orphanage/charity, or a lawful private relative arrangement with biological parents who are unable to provide care.
  2. Step 2: Preparing the Legal Petition: Retaining an enrolled advocate of the Supreme Court of Bangladesh to draft the Guardianship Petition under Section 10 of the 1890 Act before the Family Court having local jurisdiction over the child's residence.
  3. Step 3: Verification & In-Camera Judicial Examination: The Family Court judge examines the biological parents or orphanage superintendent under oath to confirm voluntary surrender without any unlawful financial transaction (child buying/selling is strictly prohibited under Section 370 of the Penal Code 1860).
  4. Step 4: Welfare Scrutiny & Home Study Review: The judge evaluates the foreign Home Study Report, medical fitness, income tax returns, and housing stability of the adoptive couple.
  5. Step 5: Delivery of Guardianship Judgment & Decree: The court issues a formal decree declaring the applicants as the permanent legal guardians, with specific permission to take the child abroad for medical care, education, and permanent residence.

4. Home Study Report & International Psychological / Financial Vetting

A cornerstone evidentiary requirement in international guardianship cases is the Home Study Report. Foreign immigration services (USCIS, UK Home Office, Immigration Canada) and Bangladeshi Family Courts will summarily refuse adoption applications without an official, certified home study conducted in the parents' country of residence:

  • Authorized Agencies: The Home Study must be prepared by a licensed, accredited adoption service provider (ASP) or local municipal social services department in the USA, UK, or Canada.
  • Scope of Investigation: Comprehensive psychological evaluation of both spouses, criminal background checks (FBI fingerprint check in the US, Enhanced DBS in the UK, RCMP check in Canada), in-person home safety inspection, financial audit (W-2s, tax transcripts, bank statements), and verification of health/infectious disease records.
  • Consular Legalization: The foreign Home Study Report must be authenticated by the Bangladesh Embassy or High Commission abroad before being submitted as evidence in the Bangladeshi Family Court.

5. The Deed of Surrender (সমর্পণ দলিল) vs Institutional Orphanage Custody

Depending on whether the child is known to the family or sourced through an institution, two distinct legal mechanisms exist:

A. Relinquishment by Biological Parents (Deed of Surrender)

If the child is born to impoverished or incapacitated biological parents who wish to relinquish custody to a relative or adoptive couple, both biological parents must execute a Registered Deed of Surrender (সন্তান সমর্পণ দলিল) before a Sub-Registrar. The deed explicitly affirms that surrender is voluntary, free from financial inducement or coercion, and that custody is transferred permanently in the best interests of the child.

B. Abandoned Infants in Welfare Institutions (Chhotomoni Nibas)

If the infant was abandoned with unknown parentage and rescued by authorities, the child is admitted to a state-run Chhotomoni Nibas under the Department of Social Services. The prospective parents must apply through the District Child Welfare Committee (শিশু কল্যাণ বোর্ড), undergo committee screening, and secure official institutional release orders approved by the Family Court.

6. Summary Matrix: Guardianship Stages, Timelines & Regulatory Authorities

The following table illustrates the complete lifecycle of adopting and immigrating a child from Bangladesh:

StageResponsible AuthorityEstimated TimelineKey Legal Deliverable
1. Foreign AccreditationForeign Adoption Agency / Home Office / USCIS2 to 4 MonthsApproved Home Study & Form I-600A / Certificate of Eligibility
2. Family Court LitigationFamily Court (Assistant / Senior Assistant Judge)1 to 3 MonthsJudicial Guardianship Order & Decree (Section 7 & 10)
3. Ministry of Social Welfare ClearanceDirectorate of Social Services (DSS), Dhaka3 to 6 WeeksOfficial Government No Objection Certificate (NOC)
4. Passport IssuanceDepartment of Immigration and Passports (DIP)7 to 14 DaysBangladeshi e-Passport in Child's Name with Guardians listed
5. Foreign Consular Immigrant VisaUS Embassy / UK High Commission / High Commission of Canada4 to 8 WeeksUS IR-3/IR-4 Visa, UK Entry Clearance, Canadian Adoption Visa
⚖️ Legal Case Evaluation & Chamber Appointment

Have your property disputes, bail matters, family issues, or litigation documents reviewed in person by Advocate Md. Shah Alam at Uttara or Dhaka Judge Court.

WhatsApp Consultation Direct Call: +880 1712-655546

7. Securing the Ministry of Social Welfare No Objection Certificate (NOC)

A critical statutory hurdle that many expatriates overlook is obtaining the Ministry of Social Welfare No Objection Certificate (সমাজকল্যাণ মন্ত্রণালয় প্রত্যয়নপত্র). Following the decree of the Family Court, the child cannot be issued a passport or cleared by immigration authorities without this certificate:

  1. Submit a formal application to the Directorate of Social Services (DSS), E-8/B-1, Agargaon, Sher-e-Bangla Nagar, Dhaka.
  2. Attach certified copies of the Family Court Guardianship Judgment, registered Deed of Surrender, foreign Home Study, adoptive parents' foreign citizenship proofs, and child's birth registration certificate.
  3. The DSS conducts background scrutiny and verifies that the child's biological mother was not paid financial consideration.
  4. The Ministry issues an official, embossed No Objection Certificate (NOC) addressed to the Director General of Immigration and Passports and the relevant foreign diplomatic mission.

8. Foreign Visa Protocols: US Embassy (IR-3/IR-4), UK Home Office & Canada IRCC

Once domestic legal processes are complete, international immigration procedures begin:

United States (USCIS & US Embassy Dhaka):

Because Bangladesh is a Non-Hague Adoption Convention country, US citizens must file under the orphan process using Form I-600A (Application for Advance Processing of an Orphan Petition) followed by Form I-600 (Petition to Classify Orphan as an Immediate Relative). Once approved, the US Embassy in Dhaka conducts a mandatory I-604 Orphan Investigation to confirm the child meets the statutory US definition of an orphan. The embassy then issues an IR-4 immigrant visa (guardianship granted for adoption in the US) or an IR-3 visa (if adoption is fully finalized).

United Kingdom (Home Office / UK Visas & Immigration):

Under UK adoption legislation, Bangladesh is a designated non-Hague nation. British parents must secure an entry clearance visa under Paragraph 314–316 of the UK Immigration Rules for intercountry adoption, requiring Home Office approval and certification from an accredited UK adoption agency before the child travels to the UK.

Canada (Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada - IRCC):

Canadian citizens must satisfy the dual-track Canadian process: (1) Approval of the Canadian sponsor by provincial adoption authorities, and (2) Child immigration or direct citizenship processing under Section 5.1 of the Citizenship Act (Canada).

9. Converting Bangladeshi Guardianship into a Full Western Adoption Decree

Because the Family Court order in Bangladesh is legally structured as a Guardianship Decree, parents residing in the United States or Canada are strongly advised to complete a Readoption (Re-adoption) in their domestic state/county family court upon arrival:

  • In the USA, filing a re-adoption petition in your local State Probate / Family Court legally seals the parent-child relationship under state law, grants the child an American birth certificate, and triggers automatic US citizenship under the Child Citizenship Act of 2000 (CCA).
  • In the UK, applying for an Adoption Order under the Adoption and Children Act 2002 vests full British nationality and creates irrevocable parental status.

10. Real-Life Case Study: US-Bangladeshi Couple Adopting from Dhaka to Texas

Background: Mr. Rafiqul and Mrs. Nasreen Haque, naturalized US citizens residing in Houston, Texas, sought to adopt their deceased brother's 2-year-old orphan daughter from Mirpur, Dhaka. The infant's mother had abandoned the child, and the family lacked financial means.

Chamber Legal Execution:

  1. Guided the Haque family in completing an accredited Home Study through an approved adoption agency in Texas, securing USCIS Form I-600A pre-approval.
  2. Executed a formal Deed of Surrender before the Sub-Registrar and filed Guardianship Case No. 34/2024 before the 2nd Family Court, Dhaka.
  3. Produced witness testimony and medical records proving the paramount welfare of the minor. The Family Court decreed legal guardianship with full permission to emigrate to the USA.
  4. Secured the Ministry of Social Welfare NOC from Agargaon, Dhaka within 4 weeks.
  5. Processed the child's Bangladeshi e-Passport and submitted Form I-600 to the US Embassy Consular Section in Dhaka.
  6. Following the I-604 field investigation, the US Embassy issued the IR-4 immigrant visa. The child arrived safely in Houston and subsequently received her Certificate of US Citizenship.

11. Fatal Legal Traps: Informal Child Handover & Human Trafficking Risks

Prospective parents must exercise immense caution against dangerous shortcuts that can trigger catastrophic criminal liability:

  • Informal Handover via Notary Stamp: An affidavit or notary public stamp claiming 'adoption' has zero legal validity in Bangladesh and is treated as international child trafficking by foreign embassies.
  • Paying Money to Biological Parents: Any monetary payment to biological parents or brokers beyond documented legal and medical expenses violates Section 370 of the Penal Code 1860, carrying sentences up to life imprisonment.
  • Falsifying Birth Certificates: Attempting to register the child's birth certificate by fraudulently listing the adoptive parents as biological parents is a criminal offense under the Birth and Death Registration Act 2004, causing immediate permanent visa blacklisting by the US Embassy and UK High Commission.

Frequently Asked Questions

Can a foreign citizen with no Bangladeshi heritage adopt a child in Bangladesh?

Yes. While Bangladeshi origin (NRB) couples are prioritized by family courts and orphanages, foreign nationals can apply for legal guardianship under the Guardians and Wards Act 1890, provided they possess a government-approved foreign Home Study and satisfy welfare standards.

How long does the entire adoption and immigration process take in Bangladesh?

The complete timeline—from Family Court guardianship filing to Ministry of Social Welfare NOC and US/UK visa issuance—typically takes between 6 to 10 months.

Does Bangladesh recognize adoption under Muslim law?

Direct adoption (severing biological lineage) is not recognized under Islamic personal law. However, Bangladeshi statutory law provides an identical practical result through Legal Guardianship under the Guardians and Wards Act 1890.

Do both prospective adoptive parents need to appear physically in the Family Court in Dhaka?

Yes. While initial filings and discovery can be handled by your appointed Supreme Court advocate, both prospective parents must personally appear in the Family Court for in-camera examination and attend the foreign embassy visa interview.

Can a single woman or single man adopt a child from Bangladesh?

Under the Guardians and Wards Act 1890, single women are eligible to apply for legal guardianship of children. However, male single applicants are generally restricted from adopting female minors under strict judicial welfare doctrines.

What is the age limit for adopting parents in Bangladesh?

While the 1890 Act specifies no rigid numerical maximum, Family Courts and the Ministry of Social Welfare generally expect prospective parents to be between 25 and 55 years of age, with at least a 21-year age difference from the minor.

Will the adopted child automatically become an American or British citizen?

For US adoptions under an IR-3 visa (or after completing state court re-adoption under an IR-4 visa), the child automatically acquires US citizenship under the Child Citizenship Act 2000. For the UK, citizenship is granted upon issuance of an Adoption Order.

Can I adopt a relative's child (niece, nephew, cousin) in Bangladesh?

Yes. Relative adoption/guardianship (intra-family) is widely practiced and favored by Family Courts in Bangladesh, provided lawful Deeds of Surrender and foreign home study clearances are established.

Affidavit Bangladesh: Purpose, Types, and How to Make One

By Advocate Md. Shah Alam · 2026-04-11 · 12 min read

⚠️ Legal Disclaimer: This article provides general legal information only and does not constitute legal advice. For advice specific to your situation, consult Advocate Md. Shah Alam directly at +880 1712-655546.

An affidavit is a sworn written statement of facts — one of the most commonly used legal documents in Bangladesh for court proceedings, government applications, property matters, and personal declarations. Understanding when you need one, what it must contain, and how to get it properly sworn and registered can save significant time and confusion.

: · Urgent Bail & Supreme Court Lawyer Dhaka

  9. Affidavit Registration: When Is It Required?
  10. Who Can Witness or Administer an Affidavit?

What is an Affidavit in Bangladesh?

An affidavit (হলফনামা in Bangla) is a written statement of facts that the maker swears under oath to be true. It is used as evidence in court proceedings and for a wide range of official purposes. Key characteristics:

  • Must be signed by the deponent (the person making the statement).
  • Must be sworn before a Notary Public, Oath Commissioner, or Magistrate — who administers the oath.
  • Once sworn, the deponent is legally bound — making a false affidavit is perjury under the Penal Code.

An experienced civil lawyer in Dhaka can prepare a legally sound affidavit for your specific purpose.

Common Uses of Affidavits

Affidavits are required or useful in numerous situations in Bangladesh:

  • Court proceedings: As evidence, in support of interlocutory applications (stay orders, injunctions), or as a substitute for oral testimony in some matters.
  • Name change: A sworn affidavit published in a national newspaper is the primary method of legally changing one's name in Bangladesh.
  • Age declaration: Where no birth certificate exists, an affidavit can establish age for official purposes.
  • Property matters: Confirming ownership, possession, or family relationships in the absence of formal documents.
  • Government/visa applications: Many embassies and government offices require sworn affidavits for specific declarations.
  • Academic purposes: Declaring equivalence of qualifications or name discrepancies in certificates.

How to Prepare an Affidavit

A legally valid affidavit in Bangladesh must contain:

  1. Heading: Court name (if court-related) or general heading.
  2. Deponent's identification: Full name, father's name, address, and NID number.
  3. Statement of facts: Clearly numbered paragraphs stating each fact. Use plain, precise language.
  4. Verification clause: A declaration that the contents are true to the best of the deponent's knowledge.
  5. Deponent's signature.
  6. Jurat clause: The section completed by the oath-administering official recording that the oath was administered, the date, and their signature and official seal.

Contact Advocate Md. Shah Alam in Uttara to have your affidavit professionally drafted and sworn.

What Happens If You Submit a False Affidavit?

Making a false statement in an affidavit sworn under oath constitutes perjury under the Penal Code 1860 (Section 191-193) — punishable by up to 7 years' imprisonment. If the false affidavit is used to defraud or commit another crime, additional charges apply. Never include anything in an affidavit that you do not know to be true.

⚖️ Legal Case Evaluation & Chamber Appointment

Have your property disputes, bail matters, family issues, or litigation documents reviewed in person by Advocate Md. Shah Alam at Uttara or Dhaka Judge Court.

WhatsApp Consultation Direct Call: +880 1712-655546

Types of Affidavits in Bangladesh

Different legal situations call for different types of affidavits. Understanding which type you need prevents rejection by courts, government offices, or embassies. The most common types include:

1. General Affidavit (Sworn Statement of Facts)

Used for: name change declarations, age confirmation, family relationship declarations, loss of documents, and general sworn statements. This is the most common type, prepared before a Notary Public or Oath Commissioner and typically does not require Sub-Registrar registration unless a specific law demands it.

2. Court Affidavit (Evidence on Affidavit)

Filed in court proceedings as evidence or in support of interlocutory applications (injunctions, stay orders, bail applications). Must follow the prescribed format under the Code of Civil Procedure Order XIX or relevant court rules. The deponent is subject to cross-examination in contested matters.

3. Affidavit of Title (Property Matters)

Used in property transactions to confirm ownership, right to sell, or absence of encumbrances. Often required by buyers, mortgage lenders, and Sub-Registrars as a supporting document to the main sale deed. Must contain specific declarations about ownership history, existing liabilities, and freedom from dispute.

4. Affidavit of Heirship / Legal Representative

Confirming who the legal heirs of a deceased person are when no formal succession certificate is available. Used by banks, RJSC, and other institutions to process accounts and shares of a deceased person pending issuance of a formal court succession certificate.

5. Affidavit for Government Offices and Embassies

Many government departments (NID office, passport office, education boards) and foreign embassies require specific sworn affidavits. These often require notarization and sometimes apostille for use abroad. An experienced advocate in Uttara Dhaka can prepare and notarize these documents with proper legal precision.

Affidavit Registration: When Is It Required?

Not all affidavits need to be registered at the Sub-Registrar's office. Understanding when registration is required (vs. merely notarized) saves time and cost:

When Registration is NOT Required

  • Name change affidavit published in a national newspaper
  • Age declaration affidavit for education or employment
  • Affidavit filed in court as evidence
  • General sworn statements before a Notary Public or Oath Commissioner

For these, a Notary Public's seal and signature (or Oath Commissioner before a Magistrate) is sufficient.

When Registration IS Required

  • Affidavits that create, declare, assign, limit, or extinguish rights over immovable property (compulsorily registrable under Section 17 of the Registration Act 1908)
  • Affidavits that form part of a registered document
  • Certain affidavits specifically required by statute to be registered

When registration is needed, the affidavit is presented at the Sub-Registrar's office with proper stamp duty, identity documents, and the required number of witnesses. The Sub-Registrar examines the document, records it, and returns a registered copy bearing the official registration number.

Stamp Duty on Affidavits

Non-judicial stamp paper is required for affidavits. The value of stamp paper varies by the nature of the affidavit and the district. For most general affidavits in Bangladesh, stamp paper of BDT 300–500 is commonly used. Property-related registered affidavits require stamp duty proportional to the property value. A lawyer can advise on the correct stamp denomination to avoid rejection.

Who Can Witness or Administer an Affidavit?

In Bangladesh, an affidavit must be sworn before an authorised person. Using an unauthorised person invalidates the affidavit. The authorised officials are:

1. Notary Public

A Notary Public is a lawyer formally appointed by the government under the Notaries Ordinance 1961 to administer oaths and attest documents. Notary Publics are commonly found in major cities — Dhaka, Chittagong, Sylhet, Rajshahi. Their seal and signature authenticate the affidavit for use in Bangladesh and internationally (for foreign purposes, apostille may additionally be required). Most general affidavits are sworn before a Notary Public.

2. Oath Commissioner

An Oath Commissioner is appointed by the Supreme Court of Bangladesh under the Oaths Act 1873 to administer oaths to persons required to make affidavits for use in legal proceedings. Oath Commissioners are typically lawyers appointed specifically for this purpose and are commonly used for court-related affidavits.

3. Magistrate or Judicial Officer

A First Class Magistrate or other judicial officer can administer oaths under the Oaths Act 1873. Affidavits sworn before a Magistrate are particularly authoritative for criminal and court proceedings.

4. Diplomatic/Consular Officers (for overseas use)

For Bangladeshis abroad who need to execute an affidavit for use in Bangladesh, the affidavit can be sworn before a Bangladeshi consular officer at the nearest Bangladesh embassy or high commission. Some countries also permit using local Notary Publics with subsequent apostille certification.

Advocate Md. Shah Alam in Uttara works with Notary Public services — contact us to have your affidavit professionally drafted, sworn, and authenticated in one visit.

Frequently Asked Questions

Can I prepare my own affidavit without a lawyer?

You can draft the content yourself, but the affidavit must be sworn before an authorized official (Notary Public, Oath Commissioner, or Magistrate). It is strongly advisable to have a lawyer draft it to ensure legal precision, especially for court proceedings.

How long does it take to get an affidavit sworn in Dhaka?

A simple affidavit can typically be sworn within the same day — visit a Notary Public with your draft, NID, and the official will administer the oath and stamp the document. For registered affidavits, the Sub-Registrar's office adds a further step.

Is an affidavit the same as a power of attorney?

No. An affidavit is a sworn statement of facts. A power of attorney authorises another person to act on your behalf. They are entirely different documents used for different purposes, though both require signing before authorized officials.

By Advocate Md. Shah Alam · 2026-03-02 ·

⚠️ Legal Disclaimer: This article provides general legal information only and does not constitute legal advice. For advice specific to your situation, consult Advocate Md. Shah Alam directly at +880 1712-655546.

If you have reason to believe you are about to be arrested, anticipatory bail in Bangladesh allows you to seek protection from custody before the arrest actually happens. Acting quickly and with the right legal guidance is critical.

What Is Anticipatory Bail?

Anticipatory bail is a legal protection that allows a person who apprehends arrest in a non-bailable offence to apply to a court for bail before they are actually arrested. If granted, the moment they are taken into custody (if at all), they are immediately released on the terms set by the court.

The concept exists to prevent misuse of arrest power — whether by police acting on a false complaint or by rivals using criminal cases as intimidation. It is particularly relevant in Bangladesh where FIRs (First Information Reports) can sometimes be filed for collateral purposes. Seek advice from a bail lawyer in Dhaka at the earliest sign of trouble.

Who Can Apply for Anticipatory Bail?

Any person who has reasonable grounds to believe they are about to be arrested in connection with a non-bailable offence may apply for anticipatory bail. Common scenarios include:

  • An FIR has been filed naming the person
  • There is news or credible information that police are seeking to arrest them
  • A case involving business/property dispute where criminal complaints are filed as a pressure tactic
  • Family disputes where one party files a false criminal complaint

The applicant must have a genuine apprehension of arrest — not a mere suspicion without basis.

Which Court Hears Anticipatory Bail?

In Bangladesh, anticipatory bail applications are heard by:

  • Sessions Court (Sessions Judge): The primary forum for anticipatory bail at the district level.
  • High Court Division: If the Sessions Court refuses or in serious matters involving complex legal questions, the application may be made directly to the High Court Division.

For urgent matters in Dhaka, filing in the High Court Division is sometimes faster than the district Sessions Court. An experienced criminal lawyer in Uttara or Dhaka will advise which forum is most appropriate given your situation.

Grounds for Seeking Anticipatory Bail

Courts consider several factors when deciding an anticipatory bail application:

  • Nature and gravity of the accusation
  • The applicant's criminal record (if any)
  • Possibility of the applicant fleeing justice
  • Whether the accusation appears to be motivated by malice or collateral pressure
  • Whether the applicant has been cooperating with the investigation
  • Risk to the investigation if bail is granted (e.g., tampering with evidence)

A well-prepared bail petition clearly addresses each of these factors in the applicant's favour.
